Thanks again for taking time today — great to learn more about SparkBridge's summarization and retrieval use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can run a scoped pilot: 

Recap from call
- Primary goal: replace current RAG pipeline with an on-prem/persistent cache-backed inference layer for customer-facing summaries (short form, average input length ~650 tokens).
- Key SLOs: p95 latency target <= 150ms for 1–8 concurrent requests per second, throughput target to sustain ~180 QPS during peak microbursts, end-to-end quality measured by editorial acceptance rate > 92%.

Recommended pilot slate (Redwood-verified profiles):
- redwood-x-7b-quant (low-cost baseline): 8-bit quantized variant, ideal for high TPS with tight p95 latency.
- redwood-x-13b (fp16): best-quality profile for your prompts; good balance of latency and output fidelity.
- redwood-xl-1.3b-8k (lightweight): fallback for cost-sensitive routes and cold-starts.

What we will share right after this thread
- Benchmarks: observed steady-TPS and latency percentiles on workloads similar to your payload (p50/p95/p99). Link to Redwood perf dashboard + CSV snapshot.
- Prompt pack: curated prompt set + suggested instruction templates for SparkBridge's summarization patterns (attached 'prompt-set-v1.jsonl').
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP): pilot scope, success criteria, timeline (attached 'sparkbridge-MAP.pdf').

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the initial pilot window (2 weeks) and the expected test dataset size (we discussed ~10k queries)?
2) Please share security contact for SOC2 checklist so we can begin the short evidence exchange.
3) We’ll provision a dedicated pilot endpoint and post our perf snapshot here by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: sparkbridge-MAP.pdf, prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — good questions. I pulled a targeted perf snapshot using a simulated retrieval+prompt workload approximating your token-length distribution. Key observed numbers (hosted Redwood Dedicated profiles):

- redwood-x-13b (fp16)
  - Steady TPS (single dedicated machine): ~120 TPS
  - p50 latency: 45 ms; p95: 130 ms; p99: 215 ms
  - Notes: highest quality in the slate, occasional latency tail under very long generations (>1.2k tokens).

- redwood-x-7b-quant (8-bit)
  - Steady TPS: ~240 TPS
  - p50 latency: 28 ms; p95: 95 ms; p99: 160 ms
  - Notes: very good for short summaries; some loss on edge-case factuality vs the 13b.

- redwood-xl-1.3b-8k (light)
  - Steady TPS: ~380 TPS
  - p50: 18 ms; p95: 55 ms
  - Notes: useful as a warm/fallback path for cost-sensitive routes.

Recommendations to hit p95 < 120ms for your common flow:
1) Primary: run redwood-x-7b-quant for user-facing low-latency summaries and QC a subset through redwood-x-13b for quality checks (sample-and-compare A/B).
2) Batching: use microbatching with a target batch size of 8 and an adaptive timeout of 10ms; this preserves latency while improving GPU utilization.
3) KV cache: enable prefix KV caching for repeated retrieval contexts (expected cache hit rate ~18–22% based on your user patterns).
4) Fallbacks: config route policy to fall back to redwood-xl-1.3b-8k when cost caps trigger autoscaler bursts.

Links & artifacts (shared):
- Perf dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/perf/dashboards/sparkbridge-2026-07
- CSV snapshot (attached): redwood-perf-snapshots-sparkbridge.csv
- Example prompt set (attached): prompt-set-v1.jsonl
